subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle design: a six-wheeled heavy carrier around 9 meters long with a turret-mounted railgun, elevated rails, and four stabilizing outrigger legs for deployment.

I'm now working out the skeleton structure with wheel and outrigger joints, then sketching the hull using panelled armor plating, decal textures for hazard stripes and unit markings, with the cab, hull body, and rear-mounted turret positioned along the chassis.

Writing part helper functions...

Still working out wheel geometry...

Now I'm adding fender plates outboard of the wheels, then blocking out the lower hull with an angled front glacis using boxes and a frustum shape, and sketching the cab as a box with a slanted glass windshield in a glowing teal tone.

Still working out outrigger stabiliser placement between the wheel axles, checking clearances along the z-axis so the legs don't collide with the wheel radius.

I'm using a "leg" role for the leg joints and "hinge" for the beam, keeping the chassis belly at a sensible height. For the rear, I'm adding two angled recoil spades dug into the ground near the back, working out the rotation and positioning so the lower edge sinks slightly below the body.

Now moving to the turret: setting up yaw and pitch joints, a ring-shaped base, drum, and cradle housing, then building out the railgun itself with breech box, paired rails, a glow strip, and coil rings spaced along the barrel.

I'm adjusting the cab dimensions to avoid clipping with the barrel rails, shrinking the cab top to 2.6 and centering it at 2.2 so everything clears properly against the hull.

Now thinking through surface detailing: hazard stripes on outrigger beams and spade, a unit emblem decal on the cab doors, stenciled "RG-6" serial text on the hull, a "DANGER HV" warning panel on the turret, and maybe a radar-style glowing screen texture on the cab side, favoring the colored texture variants over plain grey ones.

Importing glow and panelled helpers from the kit library to build the hull paint — layering a mottled olive/dark green base through panelled rivets, then blending in mud discoloration toward the lower sections using a custom paint function that mixes mud color below a height threshold with the panelled base above it.

Now I'm planning out the tire paint similarly, plus listing all the detail parts to add: side armor plates with bolt rows, tow hooks, front plough, glowing headlights, light bar, antenna and dish, smoke launchers, hatches, rear exhaust stacks, fuel tanks between wheel gaps, drive shafts, and differentials — aiming to keep the part count around 250.

I'm also planning roof sensor dome and searchlight, rear ammo/capacitor crates with straps, cable runs swept between generator and gun, a rear generator box with vents and radiator louvres, glowing red tail lights, and a rear ladder with rod rungs. Writing the cable sweep function with a fixed bone attachment to the chassis for a static pose, then setting up bone references before generating the full build code.

Now I'm designing the emblem SVG with a ring, shield, lightning bolt, and crossed rails in yellow and black, plus a stencil texture with monospace unit text in an off-white tone.

I'm also sketching out a hazard stripe pattern, a high-voltage warning sign, and a radar-style blip texture, then working through how decal planes get oriented and positioned on each face of the vehicle so text reads correctly from the viewer's side.

Confirming the -X side orientation also reads correctly, then working out the hull and wheel dimensions so the wheels sit flush against the sides without overlapping awkwardly, and planning the outrigger placement at the hull edges.

Still writing hull geometry...

Skipping long skirts since they'd overlap the wheels, I'll add fender boxes over each wheel instead with outer lip plates and mud flaps behind them, then fill the hull gaps between wheels with small armour plates near the outrigger housings.

Now I'm placing outrigger bases and front/rear plates based on wheel radius and axle positions, then setting up axle rods and differential spheres under the hull.

Writing suspension and outrigger joints...

Modeling the leg assembly...

Working out the spade plate's rotation around the hull hinge so it angles down and back for digging, calculating the X-axis rotation angle needed to orient the plate's long axis correctly.

Checking that proportion looks fine against overall height, settling on 0.12 for spike length. I'm sketching spade arm rods connecting hull to lower points, then adding a pitch pose with negative degrees to raise the bone. Now I'm setting up the railgun components on the pitch joint with a helper function for relative positioning.

Building breech box, rails, glow strip between them...

Adding recoil dampers and a danger decal on the breech side, then working through the turret's part hierarchy — figuring out how cheeks, drums, and the ammo hoist fit around the yaw bone without colliding, repositioning the capacitor drums outward to clear the cheek plates.

Adding trunnion cylinders at the pitch bone, then building the turret base with a flat torus ring, a flattened drum cylinder, and an armor skirt. I'm also routing three cable sweeps from the generator area to the breech using catmull curves on the chassis bone.

Now I'm placing a rear radiator box with grille vents, twin exhaust stacks with rain caps, plus cab details like a roof hatch, sensor dome, light bar with glowing lamps, and antenna whips at the rear corners.

Moving to the front, I'm adding headlight glow boxes on the glacis, side mirrors, angled smoke launcher tubes near the cab, door panel lines with a handle, and a glowing blue window strip on the cab sides, positioning an emblem plane near the hull side at the cab's edge.

I'm now trying to figure out where to place stencil text, since the wheels partially obscure the hull sides between them -- so I'm considering moving it to the tail face or a side skirt panel near the rear deck instead, adjusting its height to clear the wheel and fender geometry.

I'm also sketching out a front bumper assembly with a plough-style box, hazard stripe texture, tow hooks, and winch, positioning it below the glacis plate near the front of the hull.

Now I'm planning fuel tank cylinders tucked under the hull between the wheel gaps, rotated flat with retaining straps and rings, then starting to lay out rear ladder rungs along the back face of the hull.

Adding tail lights, tow pintle, and panel details on the boxes, then settling on a compact color palette for olive hull, dark steel accents, yellow trim, cyan glow, red lights, and tire rubber tones. I'm thinking through how to structure the code efficiently with mirror helpers for symmetric parts and a texture-aware part function before diving into writing it all out.

Now I'm working out a hazard-stripe SVG pattern made of slanted yellow parallelograms on a black background, plus a mottled mud paint function for the tires and an outrigger hazard plane mounted on the beam.

For the cab, I'm adding a glowing slit window beneath a brow box on the front plate, then moving on to compose everything, noting I'll only use the joints and parts and skip the unused chain/limb elements.

Still planning helper utilities: a rod function for bones and spikes, consistent hull paint for the main boxes and deck, flat metal for the wheel rims, and a ring utility for arranging lugs evenly before writing it all out.
